rationale: The buyer is identifiable — IT admins or security-conscious employees at SMB/mid-market companies on paid 1Password Business plans — and they demonstrably spend on password management already, so willingness to pay is plausible. However, this is an episodic pain (a one-time migration event driven by a PR controversy, not a recurring daily workflow problem), which keeps pain_frequency low and threatens long-term revenue if framed as a done-for-you service rather than a reusable SaaS. Operational autonomy is moderate: a structured migration guide or decision-matrix PDF/tool can be delivered automatically, but any hands-on vault export or SSO reconfiguration assistance starts pulling in human fulfillment. The deciding factor is that the demand signal is thin (21 HN upvotes from a single thread) and the controversy-driven switching intent may fade quickly — validate demand volume before investing in a build.
solution_plan: WHAT: A self-serve '1Password Business Migration Kit' — a structured, automatically delivered guide + interactive comparison checklist helping IT admins evaluate and migrate to Bitwarden Teams, Dashlane Business, or Keeper. BUILD: The factory creates a Claude-powered intake form (company size, current 1Password tier, SSO provider, compliance needs) that auto-generates a tailored migration report (PDF + web page) and a feature-parity comparison; a Stripe payment link gates the full report at ~$49 one-time, with a free teaser version for lead capture — no coding by the operator, just prompt + Typeform/Tally + Stripe + email delivery via Claude. SELL: Reach IT admins via targeted posts in r/sysadmin, r/netsec, and relevant Slack/Discord communities, plus Google Ads on 'migrate from 1Password business'; outreach copy is drafted by the factory and sent only after operator approval. MAINTAIN: Stripe billing and report delivery are automated; Claude handles support queries via a simple email parser; the operator's only recurring touch is approving the occasional outreach batch or refund. CAVEAT: Demand is controversy-driven and may be short-lived — the operator should validate with a free landing page and waitlist before paying for ads.
notes: Does not fail any build_gate on dimension scores alone, but total of 5.5 is below min_total_to_build (6.5). Stage correctly set to validate. Key risk: episodic, event-driven demand rather than recurring pain.
